BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, euschēmónōs is the word for decently, honestly. In Romans 13:13, the text says "Let us walk honestly." In 1 Corinthians 14:40, the text says "Let all things be done decently and in order."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that euschēmónōs matters because purity is not prudishness; it is keeping ourselves for the God who made us. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
